prompt: Human activity has had a negative impact on plants and animals around the world. Some people think that this cannot be changed, while others believe actions can be taken to bring about a change. Discuss both and give your opionion.
essay:
Human activity has caused serious damage to wildlife and plant life across the world. While some people believe this destruction is now impossible to reverse, others argue that effective action can still protect the natural world. Although the situation is extremely serious, I believe meaningful change is still possible if governments, businesses, and individuals act together.

On the one hand, some people think environmental damage cannot be changed because it has already gone too far. Forests have been cleared, habitats have been destroyed, and many species have become extinct as a result of human expansion. For example, when a rainforest is replaced by roads, farms, or factories, countless plants and animals lose the conditions they need to survive. Moreover, climate change and pollution continue to affect ecosystems on a global scale, making recovery slow and difficult. From this perspective, human activity has created problems that are too large and complex to solve completely.

On the other hand, there is strong evidence that action can still bring positive results. Governments can protect endangered species by creating national parks, banning illegal hunting, and punishing companies that pollute land or water. In addition, businesses can reduce environmental harm by using cleaner energy and more sustainable production methods. Individuals also have a role to play by recycling, consuming less, and supporting environmentally responsible products. For instance, conservation programmes have helped some endangered animals recover when their habitats were properly protected. Therefore, although humans have caused great damage, they also have the power to repair part of it.

In conclusion, human activity has undoubtedly harmed plants and animals, and some effects, such as extinction, cannot be undone. Nevertheless, I believe it is wrong to accept this damage as unavoidable. Strong laws, responsible industries, and public awareness can still reduce further harm and help nature recover.
